inclusion_criteria: Every reference already present in manuscript/MANUSCRIPT.md and manuscript/journal_submission/paper.tex
Primary paper or publisher/institutional record with stable DOI, arXiv ID, OpenReview ID, or repository handle
For HGCN foundations: source must define graph operations or the manifold operations used by HGCN, not merely cite them
For recent load work: 2024-2026 study must concern electric load or consumption and expose its graph definition or graph-control comparison
For evaluation work: source must directly discuss benchmark coverage, consistent pipelines, leakage, statistical testing, or strength of simple baselines
Negative and null findings are included on the same terms as positive findings
exclusion_criteria: Secondary summaries when a primary paper or accepted manuscript was available
Traffic, PV, or charging-demand papers as direct evidence for regional power-load performance; they may only serve as methodological leads
Sources whose graph construction, forecast target, or evaluation split could not be identified
Search snippets that disagreed with primary metadata
Claims of novelty, first use, absence, state of the art, equivalence, or deployment value not supported by a systematic search and matched evidence

excluded_leads.title: Short-term power load forecasting based on spatial-temporal dynamic graph and multi-scale Transformer
excluded_leads.reason: Discovered as a relevant 2025 lead, but not needed to support a unique exact claim after inclusion of closer graph-control studies.

verification_notes: The local shell had no outbound network access, so verification used the scholarly web interface and primary pages rather than a local Crossref batch script.
A third-party record for DOI 10.1016/j.ijforecast.2006.03.001 misattributed the authors; it was rejected in favor of the DOI-linked established metadata Rob J. Hyndman and Anne B. Koehler.
Citation counts were not used because they are time-varying and unnecessary for the approved objective.
No PDFs were downloaded and no claim was inferred from a title alone when method or sentence support was required.
